claims.claim: yellow perch larvae stay offshore, then commute inshore by day as they grow, and are wholly nearshore by about 30 mm TL (cited as abstract)
claims.note: No full text. The Crossref abstract describes the same sequence in Lake St. George, Ontario: early larvae offshore day and night; larger larvae and juveniles nearshore by day, offshore at dusk; the migration weakening with growth; exclusively nearshore by about 30 mm total length.

claims.claim: young perch move inshore onto the bed, where they feed on littoral invertebrates (co-cited with Werner & Hall 1988)
claims.note: The abstract supports the move inshore but says nothing of diet; it concludes the shifts are 'not in response to' prey abundance or predation risk, so it should not be cited for a food-driven move.
